finding.title: Delete or wire the abandoned AddTrackController/TrackBlueprintDraftRepository/TrackBlueprint migration trio (~1,200 dead lines)
finding.rule: Dead-code sweep + Fowler (speculative generality never adopted)
finding.why: grep across lib/ shows zero production references to AddTrackController, AddTrackFlowState, TrackBlueprintDraftRepository(+Impl), AddTrackDraft, TrackBlueprint, or ProvisionTrackUseCase outside their own files — the live wizard entry points (add_track_flow_screen.dart, track_management_hub_screen.dart, onboarding_screen.dart, track_management_body.dart) all instantiate the raw AddTrackFlow ConsumerStatefulWidget with its own hand-rolled SharedPreferences persistence and call TrackCreationService.createTrack(AddTrackResult,...) directly, never touching the typed/riverpod replacement layer. Each dead piece still has its own dedicated, passing test suite (add_track_controller_test.dart 298 lines, track_blueprint_draft_repository_impl_test.dart 115 lines, track_blueprint_test.dart 268 lines, provision_track_use_case_test.dart 460 lines = 1,141 test lines) pinning behavior nobody exercises. Worse, AddTrackController's SharedPreferences keys (_kStep='add_track_step' etc.) are byte-identical to the live AddTrackFlow's keys (_kAddTrackStep='add_track_step' etc.) — if either implementation is ever revived independently they will silently clobber each other's saved wizard state.
finding.recommendation: Delete the 6 dead source files and their 4 dedicated test files, or finish the migration and actually wire AddTrackFlow through AddTrackController/TrackBlueprint. If kept temporarily, rename one set of SharedPreferences key constants so they cannot collide.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rL for AddTrackController/TrackBlueprintDraftRepository/TrackBlueprint outside their own definition files finds a real call site, or the files are removed
test/features/track_setup/presentation/controllers/add_track_controller_test.dart and the other dead-code test files are deleted or repointed at a live call site

finding.title: Log or type the catch blocks that silently swallow errors across CurriculumActivationService/AddTrackFlow/EditTrackScreen
finding.rule: EH-3 (every catch rethrows, converts, or logs via AppLogger — no log-less catch)
finding.why: curriculum_activation_service.dart's _syncToFirestore catches ANY exception from pushing a profile's tracks to Firestore and does nothing but a comment ('Silent fail for offline/auth issues') — if the push starts failing for a persistent, non-offline reason, that profile's track state never reaches Firestore again, forever, with zero log/telemetry trail, in a codebase whose git history shows repeated real cross-device sync bugs ('eliminate active_curricula split-brain', 'sync FK crash', 'restore profile-scoped tracks'). The two stagesConfig/schedule JSON-parse catches mask malformed seeded program/stage data the same silent way. The two `on TutorWriteException catch (e)` blocks only surface the 'permission-denied' code; any other TutorWriteException code is dropped with no log and no user feedback, so a tutor-mode write failure for any other reason looks like nothing happened.
finding.recommendation: Add an AppLogger.instance.warning/error(...) call to each listed catch before continuing (even when the UI intentionally stays silent), and add an else/log branch for unhandled TutorWriteException codes.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 6 listed catch blocks logs the caught exception via AppLogger before returning/continuing
A test that throws a non-'permission-denied' TutorWriteException from the mocked service asserts a log call or a surfaced message

finding.title: Add semantic labels to icon-only pace/chazara stepper buttons
finding.why: _StepperButton (the pace +/- control in Edit Track's goal editor, wired to onPaceDecrease/onPaceIncrease) and TinyCircleButton (the chazara review-round +/- control used from chazara_widgets.dart's CustomDayEditorChip in both Add Track and Edit Track) are bare Material+InkWell+Icon with no Semantics/tooltip/label. A screen-reader user gets no spoken description — not even 'button' — for either control, so they cannot set a pace goal's numeric target or adjust a chazara delay day count with TalkBack/VoiceOver. The correct pattern already exists in the same batch: goal_cards.dart's BlurInactiveGoalOption wraps its tap target in `Semantics(button: true, label: hint, ...)`.
finding.recommendation: Wrap both widgets' InkWell in Semantics(button: true, label: <localized increase/decrease description>) or add a tooltip, matching goal_cards.dart's existing pattern.
acceptance_criteria: _StepperButton and TinyCircleButton each expose a non-empty Semantics label for their increase/decrease actions
A widget test finds a Semantics node with a button role and non-empty label at each control's location

finding.title: Replace hand-rolled ==/hashCode in TrackBlueprint's value objects with @freezed
finding.rule: Naming/placement/invariants — never hand-write ==/hashCode for data classes
finding.why: coding-standards.md is explicit: hand-rolled equality drifts from the fields and silently breaks rebuild-skipping. AddTrackDraft's hand-rolled == (track_blueprint_draft_repository.dart:66-73) proves it: it omits scopeSelectionsJson and studyDays from both == and hashCode, so two drafts differing only in scope or study-days compare equal; its own test (track_blueprint_draft_repository_impl_test.dart:95-113) only exercises equality on navStepIndex/curriculumKey/programId and never asserts inequality on the omitted fields, so the gap is untested. track_blueprint.dart repeats the same hand-rolled pattern across 6 classes and add_track_result.dart's BulkMarkIntent makes 8 sites total, even though the codebase already has a working @freezed sealed-union convention elsewhere (goal_entity.dart, sync_status.dart, restore_status.dart). Two of the three files are currently dead code (see the migration-trio finding), which caps today's practical blast radius, but the pattern remains a trap for anyone who revives them or copies the style into new code.
finding.recommendation: Convert TrackBlueprint's value objects and AddTrackDraft to @freezed sealed classes/records; add a test asserting inequality on the currently-omitted fields before/while converting.
acceptance_criteria: track_blueprint.dart and track_blueprint_draft_repository.dart's value types are @freezed with generated ==/hashCode
A test asserts two AddTrackDraft/TrackBlueprint instances differing only in a previously-omitted field are NOT equal

finding.title: Deduplicate TrackCreationService/TrackEditService's verbatim study-day persistence loop
finding.rule: Fowler duplication + DB-3 (batch()/insertAll over awaited per-row loops)
finding.why: _saveStudyDaysLocal (track_creation_service.dart:348-368) and _saveStudyDays (track_edit_service.dart:95-115) are byte-for-byte identical except a parameter name — the exact 'delete then loop-await-upsert' method copy-pasted into two sibling services. A future fix (validation, batching, a new column) applied to one copy silently leaves the other stale. Both loops (plus the unbounded _saveScopes loop) await each row individually instead of using Drift's batch()/insertAll, even though they already run inside an open transaction() so correctness is not at risk — only round-trip count.
finding.recommendation: Extract one shared DAO-level batched helper (e.g. StudyDayConfigDao.replaceAll using batch()) and call it from both services; do the same for _saveScopes.
acceptance_criteria: One shared helper implements the delete+insert study-day/scope replacement using batch()/insertAll
TrackCreationService and TrackEditService both call it; no duplicate method body remains
